review.tagline: Open book on AI agent design, with 109 runnable companion experiments
review.summary: A Chinese-language book, "Understanding AI Agents in Depth", with 10 chapters built on the formula Agent = LLM + context + tools. It covers context engineering, memory and RAG, tools and MCP, coding agents, interaction, evaluation, post-training and multi-agent collaboration. The repo holds the book sources, PDF and EPUB builds in 15 languages, and 109 Python experiments installed per chapter with uv or pip.
review.audience: Engineers learning to build and evaluate LLM agents, Chinese readers first
strengths: 109 companion experiments mapped to chapters, installable per chapter via uv.lock or pip
PDF and EPUB in 15 languages, plus an online reader
Covers evaluation and post-training (SFT/RL), not only prompting and tool use
External repos are pinned to commit SHAs for reproducible setups
weaknesses: Original text is Chinese; the other 14 translations are community-made and may lag
README says experiment code is agent-generated and not read line by line by the author
Installing or cloning does not mean an experiment was run; status is tracked separately
Most experiments need provider API keys; some need CUDA, browsers or external repos
needs: Needs Python 3.11-3.13, uv or pip, LLM provider API keys, pandoc and xelatex (only to build the PDF)
Models: Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Siliconflow
